why: Last round measured a negative: 19 of 29 real merged changes could be reverted without the project's own suite noticing. A negative is a diagnosis, not a capability. This record answers the question it leaves -- if the tests are silent, what else serves as the oracle? -- without a model, without a suite, and without a specification: run the old and new versions against the same input and report the input on which they disagree.
question: For each of 57 real merged commits in three real projects, does a bounded, change-directed differential search produce an input on which the two versions observably disagree?

method.step_1: per commit, materialise `git archive sha^` and `git archive sha` into two separate trees (no working tree, no index)
method.step_2: extract the changed non-test Python file; compare it by AST, not by diff
method.step_3: build candidate inputs from: the literals the change touches on either side, a fixed value grid, repetition shapes sized around stated limits, and strings assembled from the change's own literals
method.step_4: reach private functions through their PUBLIC entry points, found by a name-level call graph (the mechanism DiffTestGen uses and Shadow relies on), because a parameter that is a Tokenizer object cannot be driven with plain values
method.step_5: run before and after in TWO SEPARATE INTERPRETERS over the same candidates; the verdict is the first input whose returned value or exception differs
method.step_6: verify every reported witness with an INDEPENDENT script that never imports the tool, in two fresh interpreters
method.quantifier_guard: a snapshot that is imported from the wrong tree (the installed package, or the other version) aborts the run as MISLOADED_SNAPSHOT rather than reporting a divergence; a candidate that kills the runner is EXECUTION_INCOMPLETE, not 'no witness'
method.environment: python 3.11.2, no network, zero model calls

corpus.why_these: the same three projects and the same commit window as last round's revert ledger, so the two measurements can be cross-referenced commit by commit

witnesses_after_independent_verification.note: all confirmed. Confirmation is not usefulness, which is why the classes below are separate.

what_the_witnesses_actually_are.reading: A witness can be TRUE and still be worthless. `_parse_marker(0, 'ABCDEFG')` differs only because the function gained a parameter; `__version__` differs because the commit bumped it; `set_partitions` 'differed' only by a generator's memory address. The honest unit is PUBLIC_INPUT_BEHAVIOUR: an input a user could write, on a function a user calls.

{"exc": "ValueError", "msg": "Stop argument for islice() must be None or an integer: 0 <= x <= sys.maxsize."}
{"exc": "ParserSyntaxError", "msg": "Marker expression is nested more than 200 levels deep"}

the_two_measurements_together.prior_round: 19 of 29 real merged changes were revertable under the project's own suite
the_two_measurements_together.this_round: 4 of the commits that suite could not see have an input on which the versions openly disagree
the_two_measurements_together.sentence_that_survives_both: For at least four real merged fixes, there exists a specific input, generated with no model and no tests, on which the pre-fix and post-fix programs produce different results -- and the projects' own suites did not notice when the fix was removed.
the_two_measurements_together.sentence_that_does_not_survive: 'those fixes have no tests' is too strong, and so is 'the suite is broken'. The measured fact is narrower: those fixes can be reverted green, and the divergence can be found mechanically.

where_the_ceiling_is.31_of_57: NO_WITNESS_FOUND_ON_GRID -- either genuinely behaviour-preserving (most `perf(...)` commits) or the search's grid is too poor; the tool reports the bounded grid so a reader can judge which
where_the_ceiling_is.3_IMPORT_FAILED: the module could not be loaded in isolation (a runtime dependency or an import-time side effect)
where_the_ceiling_is.3_UNREACHABLE_PARAMETERS: the changed function takes objects this search cannot build
where_the_ceiling_is.7_NO_EXPRESSION_CHANGED: no computed expression and no module-level binding differs -- docs, comments, and pure annotation changes, correctly excluded

the_four_instrument_errors_that_would_ha: A runner that crashed at candidate 101 of 2,000 reported the commit as 'no witness'. Fixed by EXECUTION_INCOMPLETE.

Both versions were imported from the same path, so the 'before' run measured the 'after' file. That is a comparison of a version against itself, and it answers 'refactor' -- the most confidently wrong answer available. Fixed by MISLOADED_SNAPSHOT, strict per side.

`set_partitions` returns a generator; `repr` of a generator contains its memory address, so a docs-only commit came back with a witness. Fixed by materialising lazy results and by refusing address-bearing values.

The first witnesses were `tail(<docstring>, 0)`: literals were harvested by re-parsing `ast.dump` TEXT, which turns `Name(id='size')` into the string 'size' and puts prose and identifiers in the argument grid. Fixed by collecting real AST constants and excluding prose.
what_this_does_not_say: not that a NO_WITNESS verdict proves equivalence; it is a bounded search and the bound is reported

not that these four witnesses are the regression tests the projects should commit -- a message-only or signature-only divergence is weaker evidence than a changed value, and the classes above keep that separate
not that the search is efficient; it is cheap in money (zero) and expensive in candidates (hundreds to thousands per commit)
not a replacement for last round's ledger: the two answer different questions, and neither substitutes for the other
kill_list: using a model to judge whether a patch is correct -- not independent, and forbidden
widening the grid until a witness appears -- that fits the measurement to the claim
treating NO_WITNESS as proof of equivalence
symbolic execution or SMT: correct, and far too expensive to run before every lesson is admitted; the literal-boundary grid is the cheap shadow of the same idea
reproduce: python3 /tmp/verify_witnesses.py (per-commit archives) then python3 /tmp/independent.py (verification without the tool); the module is canonical/swe_kernel/differential_witness_v1.py, self-check with python3 -c "from canonical.swe_kernel.differential_witness_v1 import self_check; print(self_check()['passed'])"
research_grounding: Shadow of a Doubt (ICSE 2016): run old and new in one instance, emit an input wherever the versions disagree; needs no specification

DiffTestGen (arXiv 2607.16024, Jul 2026): 78.2% of PRs show behavioural differences; the gain is directed access information, not token budget; static call-graph analysis finds valid public entry points
DiffCodeGen (arXiv 2605.20473): coverage-guided differential fuzzing 'without requiring any existing tests or large language models'
